integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A continuous 10-second side-view anime fighting-game battle. Fully preserve the same two fighters, their faces, hairstyles, costumes, body proportions, the snowy mountain temple arena, the fixed 2D fighting-game camera angle, and the overall HUD layout from Picture 1. Keep the interface stable and readable throughout the entire shot. Only the health-bar values, hit effects, battle-state graphics and the final KO overlay are allowed to change.

At 0.00s, begin exactly from Picture 1. The blond male fighter in orange stands on the left and the blue-and-white female fighter stands on the right, both facing each other in ready combat stances. Both health bars are initially full. The large READY graphic quickly fades away as the fight begins.

From 0.6s to 2.2s, the male fighter launches the first clean offensive move. He quickly steps in and lands one clear solid hit on the female fighter, such as a strong straight punch or a fast kick to the upper body. A bright orange impact flash appears at the contact point, with sparks and a brief fighting-game hit-stop effect. The female fighter is pushed slightly backward with a natural reaction. At this exact moment, only the female fighter’s right-side health bar decreases. Her health bar must drop by exactly one fifth, from full health to four fifths remaining, approximately 80%. This loss must be obvious and readable. During this entire first-hit phase, the male fighter’s left-side health bar must remain completely unchanged at full. He does not lose any health at all during this section.

From 2.2s to 3.8s, the two fighters continue a short exchange of quick punches, kicks, blocks and movement feints, with arcade-style sparks, orange and blue energy trails, and subtle impact shake. The side-view camera remains stable like a classic 2D fighting game. The female fighter regains control of timing and spacing. During this exchange, the female fighter’s health remains at the previously lost one-fifth state, and the male fighter’s health still remains full until the next key hit.

Around 3.8s to 4.8s, the female fighter lands her first decisive counterattack on the male fighter. She steps inside his attack line and delivers one clear heavy strike into his torso or chest. A bright blue-white impact burst appears at the contact point, with a strong knockback reaction. At this exact moment, the male fighter’s left-side health bar begins to drop and gradually decreases from full health down to one half remaining, approximately 50%. This reduction should be clearly readable on the HUD. This is the first time the male fighter loses health in the entire sequence.

From the moment the female fighter successfully hits the male fighter and his health reaches one half, his health must then stay fixed at one half and must not change again during the following exchange section. In other words, after the female fighter’s counter reduces his HP to half, his health bar remains stable at one half until the ultimate attack begins.

From 4.8s to 6.6s, the battle continues with visually exciting but readable close-range fighting. The male fighter may still throw attacks and the female fighter may dodge, block and counter with graceful martial movement, blue motion ribbons and energy traces. Add layered fighting-game effects such as sparks, short air-pressure rings, motion streaks and minor impact flashes. However, during this entire mid-section, the male fighter’s health bar must remain unchanged at exactly one half, and the female fighter’s health bar must remain unchanged at exactly four fifths. No extra health fluctuation is allowed here.

From 6.6s to 7.8s, the female fighter creates distance and enters a clear ultimate-skill startup animation. Blue-white energy rapidly gathers around her entire body. Her hair, ribbons and flowing dress panels whip outward under intense energy pressure. A circular blue energy field expands around her. The arena lighting briefly darkens, and strong blue highlights illuminate the snow and stone floor. The HUD remains fixed and readable. During this charging phase, the male fighter’s health still stays at exactly one half and does not decrease yet.

From 7.8s to 9.2s, the female fighter explosively releases her ultimate move and dashes forward at extreme speed, producing a large sweeping blue-white energy arc, layered afterimages, and a massive final impact explosion when the attack lands on the male fighter. The male fighter is struck cleanly and violently blasted backward, then crashes hard onto the left side of the arena floor. At the exact moment this ultimate attack connects, the male fighter’s left-side health bar must go directly from the remaining one half to absolute zero. The remaining half of his health is completely emptied by this one ultimate attack. The health bar must drain all the way to empty and black, with no health left.

From 9.2s to 10.00s, the male fighter finishes falling and lies motionless in the same defeated position shown in Picture 2. The female fighter remains standing confidently on the right in the same victorious pose shown in Picture 2. A huge fiery-orange “KO” battle-result graphic bursts into the center of the screen with sparks and black brush-stroke energy. End by precisely converging toward Picture 2: male fighter knocked down on the left, his health bar completely empty, female fighter standing on the right with exactly four fifths health remaining after having lost one fifth at the beginning, large centered “KO” text, the same snowy mountain temple arena, and the same fighting-game HUD composition.

Strict health-bar logic that must be followed exactly:

1. Start: both fighters full health.
2. First key hit: male hits female → female loses exactly 1/5 HP → female remains at 4/5 HP.
3. At this time, male HP remains full and does not decrease at all.
4. Second key hit: female hits male → male HP gradually drops to 1/2.
5. After male HP reaches 1/2, it stays unchanged at 1/2 during the following exchange.
6. Final ultimate: female uses a super move → male HP goes directly from the remaining 1/2 to 0.
7. End state: female remains at 4/5 HP, male is KO with empty HP.

Maintain strict character identity, costume design, arena geometry, screen positions, portrait icons and HUD structure throughout. Do not redesign the characters. Do not change the stage. Do not introduce extra fighters. Keep the fight readable as a coherent arcade fighting-game sequence rather than random motion. Use an original anime arcade-fighting-game aesthetic only, without copying copyrighted franchise logos, exact official move names or branded elements.

overall_soundscape: Continuous high-impact arcade fighting sound design: punch and kick whooshes, sharp hit sounds, block impacts, foot slides on stone, short exertion breaths, energy charging hum, rising electrical resonance during the female fighter’s ultimate startup, and a huge final impact burst when the super move lands. Add a clear HUD-style health reduction cue when the female loses one fifth HP, another distinct heavier health-drop cue when the male drops to one half HP, and a final strong health-emptying sound when the male HP is completely drained to zero. Finish with a dramatic announcer-style “K.O.!” synchronized with the giant KO graphic. Snowy mountain wind and distant arena ambience remain subtle underneath.

non_diegetic_music: Fast-paced original arcade battle music with aggressive drums, electronic percussion and tense orchestral accents. Keep the music energetic from the opening exchange, slightly intensify when the female takes the first hit, build tension when she reverses momentum and cuts the male HP down to one half, hold strong anticipation during her ultimate charge, then hit a major climax when the super move drains the remaining half to zero, followed by a sharp victorious resolve on KO.
